data.title: Analyst Lifts Gibson Energy Price Target to $35, Reaffirming Buy on Resilient Infrastructure-Driven Cash Flows
data.description:
TD Cowen analyst Aaron Macneil maintained a Buy rating on Gibson Energy on September 1 and set a price target of C$35.00.

Aaron Macneil has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors, including a constructive outlook on Gibson Energy’s core infrastructure business and its stable cash flow profile. He views the company’s contracted, fee-based assets as providing resilient earnings, which support both a secure dividend and ongoing capital returns to shareholders.

Macneil’s rating is based on expectations for modest growth from organic projects and potential upside from disciplined capital deployment. He also sees an improved risk‑reward profile at current levels, reflected in his upward revision of the price target from $34 to $35, implying further share appreciation as execution remains solid and market fundamentals hold.

data.title: ATD Buy Rating Maintained as Analyst Lowers Price Target to C$103 Amid Near-Term Headwinds but Sees Durable Double-Digit Growth
data.description:
TD Cowen analyst Derek Lessard has maintained their bullish stance on ATD stock, giving a Buy rating yesterday.

Derek Lessard has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors tied to Alimentation Couche-Tard’s durable business model and long-term growth profile. He believes the company’s diversified mix of in-store merchandise, fuel operations, and loyalty programs, combined with structural advantages and expected synergies from the Żabka partnership, should support double-digit earnings growth over time and continued outperformance versus sector peers.

At the same time, Lessard acknowledges a softer near-term environment, with consumer trade-down behavior and regulatory changes in Europe pressuring margins and leading him to trim same-store sales and earnings forecasts, as well as reduce the price target to C$103 from C$110. Despite this more cautious short-term stance, he views ATD’s resilience, solid fuel profitability, and ability to drive spending through targeted offers and promotions as sufficient to justify maintaining a Buy recommendation, expecting the shares to benefit as consumer trends and fuel dynamics normalize.

data.title: Tyra Biosciences: Buy Rating Reiterated as SURF302 Data Upside Beckons; 12‑Month Price Target Maintained at $45
data.description:
H.C. Wainwright analyst Mitchell Kapoor has reiterated their bullish stance on TYRA stock, giving a Buy rating on August 25.

Mitchell Kapoor has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors, notably his view that upcoming SURF302 data in NMIBC is being presented with unusual transparency and confidence by management. He anticipates a strong three‑month complete response profile, with pooled CR rates at or above 70% across the 50mg and 60mg cohorts and a favorable safety profile marked by only low single‑digit rates of serious adverse events.

Kapoor also emphasizes that the current valuation gives limited credit to Tyra’s NMIBC program, creating meaningful upside if efficacy and tolerability meet expectations and later durability data are supportive. While he acknowledges downside risk if the initial readout disappoints, he maintains a 45% probability of approval for dabogratinib in urothelial carcinoma and keeps his 12‑month price target unchanged at $45, reflecting his confidence in both near‑term catalysts and longer‑term value creation.

data.title: Flex Maintained at Buy as EPC Power Acquisition Strengthens CPI Growth Ahead of Spin-Out; Price Target Unchanged at $154
data.description:
In a report released yesterday, Mark Delaney from Goldman Sachs maintained a Buy rating on Flex, with a price target of $154.00.

Mark Delaney has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors tied to Flex’s strategic expansion in power infrastructure and the EPC Power acquisition. He views EPC Power as a high-quality asset with strong positions in intelligent power conversion for data centers and grid applications, substantial installed capacity, and technology aligned with next-generation 800V architectures, which should enhance Flex’s Cloud and Power Infrastructure (CPI) segment.

Delaney also points to EPC Power’s attractive financial profile, including robust expected revenue growth, significant EBITDA margin expansion toward roughly 30%, and meaningful contribution to CPI’s earnings power. In his assessment, this deal supports Flex’s broader strategy to accelerate growth in its power portfolio ahead of the planned CPI spin-out, strengthening Flex’s competitive stance versus key peers and underpinning a favorable risk-reward at the current share price and unchanged $154 price target.
